question: A product manager is deciding whether onboarding guides, style docs, and roadmap notes for three unrelated products should live in one shared project or in three separate projects. Which approach best matches how Claude Projects are intended to be used?
options: A) Store the documents outside any project and paste the relevant ones into each new chat manually
B) Create one project per document type instead of per product, mixing all three products' content
C) Combine everything into a single project so all three products share one unified context in every chat
D) Create a separate project per product so each self-contained workspace keeps a focused knowledge base
correct_answers: D) Create a separate project per product so each self-contained workspace keeps a focused knowledge base
explanations: Incorrect. Manually pasting documents into every chat ignores the knowledge base feature that projects provide for persistent context.
Incorrect. Organizing by document type while mixing three unrelated products still blends unrelated context, the opposite of the intended focused workspace.
Incorrect. Merging unrelated products into one project would mix contexts, working against the purpose of keeping conversations focused.
Correct. Projects are designed as self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases, so organizing by unrelated product keeps context focused and avoids cross-contamination.
